quarterly_data.signal: Dell's 10-Q: revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was approximately $132 billion as of July 31, 2026, of which Dell expects to recognize approximately 77% as revenue in the next twelve months and approximately 14% in the following twelve months. ISG benefitted from substantial demand for AI-optimized servers, resulting in a significant increase in backlog as Dell exited the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO approximately $132 billion (July 31, 2026); approximately 77% in next twelve months, approximately 14% in following twelve months

quarterly_data.signal: Purchase obligations (which the 10-Q says are primarily related to commitments with suppliers, software maintenance, and support services) were $34.8 billion as of July 31, 2026, with $24.6 billion payable within twelve months; Dell increased purchases of certain components to meet growing demand and expects those purchases to keep increasing, including committed purchases under long-term strategic supplier agreements at prices to be mutually agreed upon at a future date (portions of which are excluded from purchase obligations). Dell also issues financial guarantees to suppliers for components bought directly by its contract manufacturers; maximum potential future payments under these guarantees were $8.6 billion, with full recourse against the contract manufacturers.
quarterly_data.figure: purchase obligations $34.8 billion, $24.6 billion payable within twelve months; supplier financial guarantees for contract-manufacturer purchases up to $8.6 billion (July 31, 2026)
